record.title: The Drowned Street
record.premise: The Chime-Keepers' elder of Toklea trades the keystone's story for her family's grave-stake, which the player raises from a chest in the drowned street of Zul-Etha past its crocodiles, and the elder names the knights' tomb at Eurydike.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 8. Kept: the elder in the Kothringi Greathouse (Toil's End's one interior), her price (her family's grave-stake from a chest in Zul-Etha's drowned street), the crocodiles and the old bull on the roof peaks, the three ways (kill from a roof or from range, calm with Illusion, swim under unseen), and her naming the knight-captain's tomb at Eurydike. Filled: the elder's name (Hums-the-Long-Note), that the stake stays hers (the hand-in takes it), and the report to Nesh-Deeka the brief asks for, where she already knows the Unbound have been asking Gideon's diggers about Eurydike.

truth.what: When the carts stopped, a Chime-Keeper family lodged its ancestor's carved grave-stake in a chest in the street to carry later; the washes drowned the street first.
A Natai fisherman saw the chest; the crocodiles keep everyone off.

facts.claim: Hums-the-Long-Note will tell what the keystone opens once her family's grave-stake is raised from the chest in the drowned street of Zul-Etha.
The keystone opens the tomb of the knight-captain at Eurydike; the Kothringi knights of Gideon were the last to guard the kings' road to the Root.
The Unbound have been asking Gideon's diggers about Eurydike.

stages.journalText: Nesh-Deeka sent me with the keystone to the Chime-Keepers of Toklea, who keep what is left of Kothringi lore. I'm to show it to their elder in the Kothringi Greathouse.
stages.directions: Poles-Upriver's boats run from Helstrom to Blackrose and on to Lujei Ferry. From the ferry's raft, cross the channel north to Toklea, the town on stone footings where chimes hang from every eave; the greathouse is the old Kothringi hall in the middle.

objectives.objectiveText: Show the keystone to the elder of the Chime-Keepers in Toklea.

information.going: The keystone from the wreck is Kothringi; the Chime-Keepers' elder may know what it opens.
information.next: Take boats to Lujei Ferry, cross to Toklea and show the keystone to the elder in the Kothringi Greathouse.

stages.journalText: Hums-the-Long-Note knows the keystone, and named her price: her family's carved grave-stake lies in a chest in the drowned street of Zul-Etha, and she wants it raised. Crocodiles lie on the roof peaks above it. I may kill them from a roof or from range, calm them with Illusion, or swim under them unseen to the chest.
stages.directions: Take a boat from Blackrose to Mir-Xal's river quay, then walk south-east into the washes to three roof peaks standing out of green water; the chest lies in the street below them.

objectives.objectiveText: Raise the grave-stake from the chest in Zul-Etha's drowned street.

information.going: The elder will say what the keystone opens if I raise her family's grave-stake.
information.next: Go to Zul-Etha and take the grave-stake from the chest under the water.
information.ways: Kill the crocodiles (from a roof or from range), calm them with Illusion, or swim under them unseen.

stages.journalText: I raised the grave-stake from the drowned street. I'm to bring it to Hums-the-Long-Note in the Kothringi Greathouse in Toklea.

objectives.objectiveText: Bring the grave-stake to Hums-the-Long-Note in Toklea.

information.going: I have the stake; the elder owes me the keystone's story.

stages.journalText: Hums-the-Long-Note took her family's stake and kept her word: the keystone opens the tomb of the knight-captain at Eurydike, a ruin near Gideon. The Kothringi knights of Gideon were the last to guard the kings' road to the Root. I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom.

objectives.objectiveText: Tell Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom what the keystone opens.

information.going: The keystone opens the knight-captain's tomb at Eurydike, on the old road to the Root.

stages.journalText: Nesh-Deeka heard me out. She already knew that the Unbound have been asking Gideon's diggers about Eurydike. When I asked how, she said "we listen" and told me to hurry. She paid me 100 gold.

information.going: The Unbound are close behind on the same trail; Nesh-Deeka knows it and will not say how.
information.next: MN09 starts; its first entry marks Eurydike.

stages.journalText: Nesh-Deeka is dead. Nobody else in the Toh-Reel-Ka knows me, and the trail of the Eye ends with her.

information.going: The one the hunt for the Eye depends on is dead; the main quest cannot go on.
information.next: Nothing more in the main quest.

stages.journalText: Hums-the-Long-Note is dead. The other Chime-Keepers say only the elder knew the keystone; it was carved for a door "near Gideon, where the knights lie". I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom.

objectives.objectiveText: Tell Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom what the Chime-Keepers said.

information.going: The elder is dead but the keystone's door lies near Gideon where the knights lie.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Hums-the-Long-Note, elder of the Chime-Keepers; she keeps the old Kothringi songs and the chimes that carry them; Umbriel, in a line: the dead of the flying city came down even here, and the chimes rang for days. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Do you know this keystone?
topics.intent: Hums-the-Long-Note. Tells: she does, but a song is paid for. Her family's carved grave-stake lies in a chest in the drowned street of Zul-Etha, a carting village the washes drowned, reached from Mir-Xal's quay by walking south-east; crocodiles and an old bull lie on its three roof peaks. Kill them from a roof or with arrows, calm them with Illusion, or swim under them unseen. Raise the stake and she will tell. Does: sets stage 20.

topics.label: Here is your family's grave-stake.
topics.intent: Hums-the-Long-Note. Tells: the keystone opens the tomb of the knight-captain at Eurydike, a roofless Kothringi hall a short walk north of Gideon. The Kothringi knights of Gideon were the last to guard the old kings' road to the Root; their captain was buried with what marked the way. Does: sets stage 40, whose start takes the stake.

topics.label: Who were the knights of Gideon?
topics.intent: Hums-the-Long-Note. Tells: Kothringi who served in Gideon's garrison in the Second Era and kept the road the priest-kings used to the Root; the flu killed them with all their people, and their dead are said to walk their hall still. Does: nothing.

topics.label: The keystone opens the knight-captain's tomb at Eurydike.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: good; the Unbound have been asking Gideon's diggers about Eurydike, so the player must be quick. Does: nothing (a question; its answer is topic.mn08-how-know).

topics.label: How do you know what the Unbound ask in Gideon?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: "We listen." She tells the player to hurry, and pays 100 gold. Does: sets stage 90.

state.notes: I am a Voh-Vastei of the Toh-Reel-Ka under Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom. Hums-the-Long-Note, elder of the Chime-Keepers in Toklea, told me the Kothringi Keystone opens the knight-captain tomb at Eurydike, a roofless Kothringi hall a short walk north of Gideon. The knights of Gideon guarded the old kings road to the Root, and the captain was buried with what marked the way. I paid her price by taking her family grave-stake from the chest in drowned Zul-Etha, without fighting the crocodiles. I reported to Nesh-Deeka, who paid 100 gold (about 700 total). She says the Unbound are already asking Gideon diggers about Eurydike, so we must be quick. She only said "we listen" about how she knows. I still carry the Keystone, Pale Harvest Strongbox Key, Old Silver Setting, The Collector note and the smuggler key. Open questions: what the Eye and the Root are, and what the tomb holds. The Collector (Ennodius Vanin) and the Unbound are still hunting. Next: go to Eurydike quietly and open the tomb.

know_text: I am a Voh-Vastei of the Toh-Reel-Ka under Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom. At the Pale Harvest wreck I killed the Drowned Captain, took his key and opened the strongbox. It held a Kothringi Keystone, which I still carry along with the Pale Harvest Strongbox Key, the Old Silver Setting, The Collector note and the smuggler key. I have about 600 gold after Nesh-Deeka paid me 100. She does not know the keystone, but she says it is Kothringi. The Chime-Keepers of Toklea, on the river fork in the Tulmek Washes, keep Kothringi lore, and their elder should know it. She says the Unbound have not found the wreck, but she will not say how she knows ("we listen"). The Collector (Ennodius Vanin) and the Unbound are still hunting the Eye. I have not yet asked her about the Kothringi or the Chime-Keepers. Next step: go to Toklea and show the keystone to the elder.
